title: I'm building a farming RPG for handhelds with AI tools. Another Day in Heaven has a free alpha
author: Think-Shoulder-4960
selftext:
Hey everyone, I'm the solo dev behind TyR Games. Some of you might know me as Tyr4nTX from Nexus Mods. I've put out a free alpha of Another Day in Heaven, a Godot game that mixes farming and everyday village life with real-time squad combat.



The idea is pretty simple: grow a farm, dig up ore, make your own gear, then head out with your companions. There are six life skills covering farming, animals, forestry, mining, trading and smithing. At Berta's forge you actually time the hammer strikes to make weapons and armour. You can create your farmer, spend attribute points and sort out your squad's equipment in the Roster Book. There are also people to get to know, including Valeska and the sisters Mila and Tessa. Combat has seven weapon specials on the controller's Y button, from Frost Nova to Dragonflight. I might be a little too pleased with that last one :)



Since this is r/aigamedev, here's where AI fits in. I use AI-assisted tools for parts of the code, art, audio and writing, alongside licensed assets. For character portraits, my rule is to work from an approved reference and keep the same face, proportions and outfit identity across expressions. Getting a nice single image is only one part of it; checking the variants, transparent edges and how they look inside the game matters too. On the code side, I'm putting a lot of emphasis on shared combat rules and checking what actually happens on screen. Mine combat and squad battles need consistent stats, even though you play them differently.



The big focus for me is handheld play. I'm designing around Steam Deck and ASUS ROG Ally: controller navigation, readable menus at 1280 × 800, and clear button prompts. Keeping text separate from decorative UI art also makes the English/German layouts much easier to work on. There's a native Linux/SteamOS build as well as Windows. Physical testing on Deck and Ally is still pending, so this isn't a Steam Deck Verified claim.



It's a playable alpha with rough edges, including some unfinished English UI text. You can download it for $0; tips are optional and everyone gets the same build.



If you're building with AI too, how are you checking consistency once several systems have to work together? And if you try mine, I'd love to hear where the controller flow gets awkward.

[Download the free alpha on itch.io](https://tyr4ntx1.itch.io/another-day-in-heaven)

[Watch the gameplay trailer on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ptTBwLKBVfg)

comments.author: The-Cliff-Of-Traps
comments.body:
Okay, played some of it. By that I mean what I could. I'll expand on that.

Point one, I was not expecting to be basically assaulted with boobs just downloading it. So uh... You got that I guess.

Okay though serious stuff, I didn't play through a lot. Basically just made it to where Berta is telling you to smash two stones and then she says something about one stone being the one.

Primary reason I didn't go beyond that was the language barrier. Most of this isn't in english and I don't speak or read anything but that so that made things a bit difficult.

Two I'm not sure if it was an issue of me not completing some invisible check mark but I could not get this box above the hot bar which was saying how to switch between items and what left and right click do to close. It was there the moment it appeared and did not leave. 

Three, maybe drop some of the stardew valley stuff. I'm not saying you copied everything... But I'd be lying if I said it isn't basically a copy of it. Especially the image you have shown here, I thought this was going to be a stardew valley but with a different art style. Starting, on what is a plot of land that's abandoned, similar character designs (that aren't the detailed arts shown when talking which to my understanding can be divided by - Boobs, boobs, boobs, no boobs, boobs. Probably tone it down a little.), farming turnips, with a mostly overgrown land with rocks you can break and trees you can chop. That's basically the start of stardew valley one to one.

So probably see about changing the start a little bit, but otherwise it isn't bad. What I could play anyway. But, and this is a big one, I enjoyed it because its basically just stardew valley.

The biggest issue, namely the language problem, can be easily resolved. Just prompt the A.I. to make an optional translation of everything into english with a prompt on the title screen about what language you want.
